HIS102 – Abs3
The teacher’s voice is a bit slow, but he teaches very well. First, let’s talk about the contents of HIS102. This course mainly covers ancient world civilizations and global transformations during the Middle Ages, such as the Renaissance and the Industrial Revolution. The sir explains every topic thoroughly using the slides. However, since his voice is a bit slow, it’s better to sit in the front row to stay focused.
Now about the exam pattern:
The quizzes are MCQs. Out of 3 quizzes, the best 2 will be counted. The questions are a mix of easy, medium, and hard. To get full marks (20 out of 20), you need to follow both the slides and his class lectures carefully. Otherwise, scoring high becomes difficult.
If it’s noticed that students are not scoring well in quizzes, then the third quiz is sometimes taken in the form of short questions.
Now about the midterm and final exams:
For broad questions, sir usually gives suggestions, and questions appear exactly from those suggestions. For short questions, you’ll find some listed at the end of each chapter in the slides — the questions come from there. If you can write well, sir gives good marks.
There is one presentation. You should do it properly. The sir appreciates class participation, so try to engage — it can make you one of his favorites.
Grading is fair. No curve, no de-curve.

Faculty Reviews:
Intersession 2023
RAK (Ms Rashida Akter Khanum)
PHI101.2 (ST 11:15am)
The chillest course ever with the chillest faculty ever. Philosophy may sound a bit intimidating, but it won’t be with her. The content we covered was very little. I basically had to study only the parts of topics I would actually be writing about in the exam. Miss all but tells you the exact questions she will set in the exams. You don’t have to study everything covered in class. There will be 2 quizzes (best 1), a midterm, and a viva. Quizzes will have only mcqs, and the mid/final will require you to write two broad questions. The viva will be just like the mid/final, and you’ll have to say your answers in short.
CNP (Mr Chandra Nath Podder)
MAT130.3 (ST 2:30pm)
Sir may initially come off as intimidating and unhelpful, but he isn’t. He likes participation, active effort, and knowing the basics. He took 6 quizzes (said he usually takes as many as he can), and I’m not sure but I think he counted the best 4. There is also a mid, and two assignments which are fairly small. He solves particular problems in class, and questions are exactly like those. Studying class notes and assignment problems is enough. No slides or handouts, so take note of everything he says and writes (which isn’t too much either). It’s a fairly easy course with virtually nothing new to learn, other than some trigonometric integration in the beginning, just using previous knowledge of calculus to solve practical problems.

Suggest the Best Faculty for phi101 in terms of grading.
